breakfast.name: Żurek (Polish Sour Rye Soup)
breakfast.description: Traditional Polish sour rye soup made from fermented rye flour starter, served with sausage and hard-boiled eggs. A distinctive soup with tangy flavor from fermentation
ingredients: 2 cups fermented rye flour starter (żur zakwas)
instructions: Strain fermented rye starter through fine mesh to remove solids
Heat stock in large pot and bring to boil
Reduce heat and add strained rye starter, stirring well
Add sausages (whole or sliced), garlic, marjoram, and black pepper
Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often
Season with salt and pepper to taste
Place 2 egg halves in each bowl
Top with sausage pieces and ladle soup over eggs
Serve with rye bread on the side
breakfast.notes: Żur zakwas (fermented rye starter) can be purchased at Polish delis or made at home by fermenting rye flour for 5 days. Without it, authentic żurek cannot be made
breakfast.fun_fact: Żurek is traditionally eaten at Easter but is enjoyed year-round in Poland. The fermentation creates the soup's hallmark sour flavor that defines authentic żurek
alternatives: Make vegetarian with beans instead of sausage
